alternatives_considered: A single all-industry office-administration market was rejected as overbroad because the manual expressly includes named medical, dental, hotel, and motel administration labels while excluding complete-operation models.
A vertical-operator boundary was rejected because the manual definition excludes providing operating staff for complete business operations.
Product-line identities were not treated as markets solely because they were reported as products sold by NAICS 561110.
analysis_summary: The frozen manual defines NAICS 561110 as contracted day-to-day office administrative services for others and expressly excludes complete-operation staffing. The evidence supports a horizontal outsourced-office-administration market, with medical and dental administration retained as provisional vertical boundary candidates because the index names them. Hotel and motel administration remain inside the horizontal service boundary only when they do not provide complete operation of the client business. All listed NAPCS identities are source product identities rather than equivalent operating-market identities in this family.

proposed_markets.acquisition_universe: Providers selling outsourced, contract or fee-based multi-function office administration to client organizations.
aliases: Business management services except complete operation
proposed_markets.ambient_ai_workflow: AI may automate billing, recordkeeping, scheduling, personnel administration, workflow routing, document handling and client-service coordination; specific adoption is not evidenced.
proposed_markets.boundary: Includes providers delivering a range of day-to-day office administrative services for others on contract or fee. Excludes complete operation of a client business with operating staff, holding-company functions, corporate managing offices, computer facilities management, construction and farm management, real-estate property management, food-service contracting, and advisory-only management consulting.
proposed_markets.definition: Contracted provision of a range of day-to-day office administrative services, including financial planning, billing and recordkeeping, personnel, and physical distribution and logistics, without operating staff for complete client-business operations.
proposed_markets.delivery_model: Ongoing contract or fee-based outsourced administration.
proposed_markets.economics_risk: Commercial model and allocation of client-operating risk are not directly stated; complete-operation staffing is expressly outside boundary.
explicit_exclusions: Complete operation of a client business with operating staff
Holding companies and corporate managing offices
proposed_markets.job_to_be_done: Run recurring client office administration without assuming complete operation of the client business.
proposed_markets.workforce_model: Administrative-service personnel; not operating staff for complete client-business operation.

research_gaps.current_judgment: Medical and dental labels support provisional vertical candidates, while hotel and motel labels remain included only where services do not constitute complete operation. The frozen evidence does not establish whether these vertical labels represent distinct buyer, workflow, workforce, or economic markets rather than vertical sales segments of horizontal office administration.
research_gaps.question: Do medical, dental, hotel, motel, and other named administration models have sufficiently distinct buyers, jobs, delivery models, workforce, risk allocation, acquisition universes, and AI workflows to split from horizontal outsourced office administration?
research_gaps.retry_trigger: Obtain frozen evidence directly describing scope of work, buyer, contracting, workforce, and whether each named model provides only administration or complete operation.

research_gaps.current_judgment: The frozen pack contains no direct evidence for Ambient AI workflow, pricing, client-risk allocation, or workforce composition beyond exclusion of operating staff.
research_gaps.question: What workforce mix, risk allocation, commercial model, and AI-enabled workflow characterize outsourced office administration and its provisional medical and dental variants?
research_gaps.retry_trigger: Obtain frozen operating-model evidence addressing staffing, contractual responsibility, pricing, workflow systems, and AI use.
